plumes.visual_description: narrow semi-transparent gray horizontal veil extending westward from the large island over dark ocean, distinct from brighter white cumulus and cirrus to the north and south

per_plume.source_hint: tracked trailing end in open ocean ~370-405 km from summits; no vent or fire alignment
evidence: USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW in episodic_pause (episode 55 fountaining ended Oct 17, episode 56 forecast Oct 30-Nov 5) and Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, so no active eruptive source for fresh vog. [E1]
No FIRMS fire clusters in Hawaii box on 2026-10-25, arguing against wildfire smoke. [E6]

Wind at plume centroid from 42 deg at 18.1 km/h (blowing toward ~222 deg SW) while tracked plume drift is toward 129 deg SE at ~18.2 km/h with fit R2 0.59; ~93 deg disagreement contradicts simple downwind transport from the island and lowers confidence. [E2, E5]

Tracked inferred source end lies at 19.975N, 159.11W in open ocean ~405.6 km from Kilauea and ~370.7 km from Mauna Loa, not trailing from either vent; geometric upwind end assuming wind would be near the islands (~69-85 km) but actual motion places trailing end to the west. [E5, E7]

Mask is 377 km long, 4486 km2, only 2.5% over land and not swallowing islands (reliable over dark ocean), appearing as faint thin gray translucent veil distinct from surrounding bright white cumulus/cirrus, consistent with either thin cirrus or dilute aged haze but not diagnostic. [E3, E4]

evidence_cited.text: USGS HVO at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW in episodic_pause (episode 55 fountaining ended Oct 17, episode 56 forecast Oct 30-Nov 5) and Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, so no active eruptive source for fresh vog.
No FIRMS fire clusters in Hawaii box on 2026-10-25, arguing against wildfire smoke.

Wind at plume centroid from 42 deg at 18.1 km/h (blowing toward ~222 deg SW) while tracked plume drift is toward 129 deg SE at ~18.2 km/h with fit R2 0.59; ~93 deg disagreement contradicts simple downwind transport from the island and lowers confidence.

Tracked inferred source end lies at 19.975N, 159.11W in open ocean ~405.6 km from Kilauea and ~370.7 km from Mauna Loa, not trailing from either vent; geometric upwind end assuming wind would be near the islands (~69-85 km) but actual motion places trailing end to the west.

Mask is 377 km long, 4486 km2, only 2.5% over land and not swallowing islands (reliable over dark ocean), appearing as faint thin gray translucent veil distinct from surrounding bright white cumulus/cirrus, consistent with either thin cirrus or dilute aged haze but not diagnostic.

classify.caveats: Kilauea in episodic pause and Mauna Loa quiet, ~90 deg wind vs tracked-drift mismatch, and far-ocean inferred source prevent confident vog/cloud call; aged vog or thin cirrus cannot be excluded.

kilauea.activity_summary: The Halema'uma'u eruption of Kīlauea is currently paused after episode 55 fountaining ended on October 17. Summit reinflation continues today and the forecast for episode 56 fountaining is between October 30 and November 5, 2026. Overview: The summit eruption of Kīlauea in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused following lava fountaining in episode 55 on October 17, 2026.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
